clue.text: Guardian to city of Swiss composer

parts.note: the newspaper speaks of itself in the editorial first person plural, we
Bern is the Swiss capital city

explanation.surface: A Swiss musician is posted to a city by the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian's leader columns say 'we', so the paper's name gives WE. Webern was in fact Austrian; 'of Swiss' belongs to the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Anton Webern was a twentieth-century Viennese composer of the Second Viennese School.

clue.text: Two clubs said to be dropped by Tony in 21

indicators.note: this word signals that the clubs are spoken and the answer sounds like them

parts.note: a wedge and a wood are both golf clubs

explanation.surface: Two golf clubs are dropped by someone called Tony in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Benn, the Labour politician, renounced his peerage and dropped his name Anthony Wedgwood Benn; 21 is CHINA SHOP, and Wedgwood china is what gets dropped there.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedgwood is a famous make of English china, and the middle name Tony Benn stopped using.

clue.text: Boat people need lawyers to get lowdown about setter

parts.note: barristers collectively are the Bar

indicators.note: the information word goes round the setter's pronoun

parts.note: gen is British slang for information, the lowdown
the crossword setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: Refugees at sea need lawyers to brief them on the puzzle-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boat people' suggests refugees but simply means those who work barges.
explanation.definitionFit: Bargemen crew canal and river barges, so they are literally people of boats.

clue.text: Oriental bird lay back in list found in 21

indicators.note: the reversed run goes inside the list word

parts.note: a roster is a list of names on duty

indicators.note: the run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: E for East, the Orient
a crow is a bird
taken as written

explanation.surface: An eastern bird lays an egg on a duty list in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the eastern bird and 'lay' as one run, which 'in' sets inside the list. 21 is CHINA SHOP; Royal Worcester is an English porcelain make.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Worcester porcelain is a well-known English china brand found in such shops.

clue.text: I don't want an article of gold

parts.note: an article is a thing or item, an object
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Someone refuses a piece of gold jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who protests or dissents is the one saying they do not want something.

clue.text: Swapped wife for red deer and rabbit?

indicators.note: for here means in exchange for, so the animal letters are swapped into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man trades his wife for some deer and a rabbit.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of RED DEER and RABBIT gives the title of Smetana's comic opera; the question mark marks the loose anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bartered bride is a wife traded away, and the title of Smetana's opera.

clue.text: Amphibian, nice if working inside, is working well

indicators.note: the anagrammed letters go within the amphibian word

parts.note: an eft is a newt

indicators.note: letters working are moving around into a new order

explanation.surface: A newt is working nicely in some job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' appears twice: first it signals the anagram, then 'working well' is the definition; 'inside' puts the rearranged letters within the newt.
explanation.definitionFit: Being efficient means functioning productively with little waste.

clue.text: Boy has his number increased by 995: that will shake him

indicators.note: his Roman numeral, worth five, rises by 995 to the numeral worth a thousand

parts.note: Trevor is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad's figure jumps by nearly a thousand, which will give him a jolt.
explanation.walkthrough: V is Roman 5; adding 995 makes 1000, Roman M.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is a shaking or quivering, something that shakes a person.

clue.text: Clothes etc around the Row when doing this?

definitions.text: Clothes etc around the Row when doing this?

indicators.note: the clothing word goes round the noise word

parts.note: a rig is an outfit or set of gear
a row is a din, a loud noise

explanation.surface: What one wears going along Rotten Row on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: Rotten Row is the sandy track in London's Hyde Park used for horse riding, so the whole clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding clothes are worn on Rotten Row, the Hyde Park bridle path.

clue.text: See 12
Farmland unfriendly, accepting sailors' say so?

annotationWithheld.why: Farmland unfriendly, accepting sailors' say so? (9): COLD round RN leaves FIE unexplained; no sense of 'say so' gives FIE
annotationWithheld.clue: Farmland unfriendly, accepting sailors' say so?

clue.text: Labour politician and Conservative placed apart in making of domino effect

indicators.note: the politicians go inside the word for making rather than beside it
the two politicians are set apart from each other, each going into the making word at its own point

parts.note: creation is the act of making
Peter Hain is a Labour politician

explanation.surface: A Labour man and a Tory are kept apart while some knock-on effect develops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'placed apart' means the Labour and Tory pieces go 'in' the making word at separate points, so the Tory letter lands inside REACTION's middle, not beside the Labour man.
explanation.definitionFit: A domino effect is a sequence where each event triggers the next, the same idea as a chain reaction.

clue.text: Man — island — 's (between you and me) between axles

indicators.note: the bracketed words say the other pieces sit between the two letters for 'you and me'

parts.note: you and me together are we
a man is he
Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile
the possessive ending supplies its letter

explanation.surface: A fussy clue-writer interrupts himself to whisper something about an island's man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like the Isle of Man beside 'island', but is just a pronoun; 'between you and me' looks like a confidential aside but is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The distance between a vehicle's front and rear axles is its wheelbase, a motoring term.

clue.text: 3 race found in 21

parts.note: the answer at 3 is royal, and a crown is the royal emblem
the Derby is the famous English flat horse race at Epsom

explanation.surface: A royal horse race is said to be found in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is CHINA SHOP; Royal Crown Derby is a famous make of English porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Crown Derby porcelain is a make of fine china sold in a china shop.

clue.text: Got to spring down river Tees (detail incorrect)

indicators.note: letters set down incorrectly are in the wrong order, so these are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: read as de-tail: the word loses its tail, its final letter

explanation.surface: A traveller went down the River Tees, with some detail wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detail' cuts TEES to TEE; 'incorrect' then rearranges DOWN, RIVER and TEE. The Tees is a river in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: To survive or stay through winter until spring arrives is to have spent the winter there.

clue.text: See 3
A record has Latin letters

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record
habet is the Latin for has

explanation.surface: A gramophone disc includes some Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: An alphabet is the full set of letters used to write a language.

clue.text: Woodlouse's music player goes round like this article

indicators.note: the player name encircles the words for like this

parts.note: an iPod is a portable music player
so means in this way, like this
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A woodlouse's gadget spins, much like this item.
explanation.walkthrough: Woodlice belong to the crustacean order Isopoda, and the adjective describes them.
explanation.definitionFit: Isopodan describes the isopods, the crustacean order to which woodlice belong.

clue.text: Agree to drop a note to extreme small boy to temporary hangers on wall

annotationWithheld.why: Agree to drop a note to extreme small boy to temporary hangers on wall (5,7): GREE from agree less A is clear, but no reading of 'note to extreme small boy' yields NBOTTLES
annotationWithheld.clue: Agree to drop a note to extreme small boy to temporary hangers on wall

clue.text: Revolutionary spy has revolutionary soul

indicators.note: turned over or in revolution, the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: A rebel agent shares quarters with a rebel spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Revolutionary' rearranges SPY to PSY; the second is Che Guevara.
explanation.definitionFit: Psyche means the human soul or mind, from the Greek word for breath and spirit.

clue.text: Carnivore of former years at sea?

annotationWithheld.why: Carnivore of former years at sea? (6): BC inside BOAT gives the letters, but 'at sea' must be both the container indicator and the boat
annotationWithheld.clue: Carnivore of former years at sea?

clue.text: Special poem found in 21

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A special poem turns up in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is CHINA SHOP; Spode is a famous Staffordshire pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: Spode is an English make of porcelain and earthenware sold in china shops.

clue.text: Meat keeps in wood, which is no place for a bull

indicators.note: the meat word holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: a chop is a cut of meat
taken as written
ash is a kind of wood

explanation.surface: A butcher stores meat in a wooden box, though a bull would be out of place.
explanation.walkthrough: A bull in a china shop is the proverbial clumsy blunderer.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'a bull in a china shop' makes such a shop the worst spot for a bull.

clue.text: Defence of one ending a party

indicators.note: one is placed at the close of the other pieces

parts.note: Lib is short for the Liberal party
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: One person brings the curtain down on a party, in self-defence.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a defence in law that the accused was somewhere else at the time.

clue.text: It's said being ill for a short time creates a scar

indicators.note: these words signal that the phrase is spoken and the answer sounds like it

parts.words: being ill for a short time
parts.note: being ill is being sick, and a short time is a trice, as in 'in a trice'

explanation.surface: Someone claims a brief illness leaves a mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicatrice is a medical and literary word for the scar left by a healed wound.

clue.text: Being ill like a flower?

definitions.meaning: someone poorly is laid up under the covers
a garden flower grows in a flowerbed

explanation.definitionFit: A sick person stays lying down at home, while a flower is planted in a garden plot.

clue.text: Most of 10th, right, plus 1 and 12?

indicators.note: the word loses one letter, keeping most of it

parts.note: the ordinal tenth
one is the number written as a word

explanation.surface: A ceremony takes most of the tenth, the right plus a couple of other numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops the first T of TENTH, leaving ENTH. 12 is CROWN, here read as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To place a monarch on the throne is to crown them, a synonym in the verb sense.

clue.text: Herb added, found in 21

parts.note: mint is a garden herb
on means added, as in 'tacked on'

explanation.surface: A herb is added to something found in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is CHINA SHOP; Minton is a famous Stoke-on-Trent porcelain maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Minton is a make of English bone china and tiles, stock for a china shop.
